_comment: Gauntlet Loop live status, Phase C (Stream C — visual, bar v2). Written after every checkpoint, not just at completion, per the skill's Step 3. If a session dies mid-round, this file says exactly how far it got instead of leaving silence. Narrative record lives in docs/VISUAL_UPGRADE_NOTE.md; this is the machine-readable tip.
budgetMode: subscription — builder is the main thread, subagents are critics only, pieces run sequentially

doesNotGovern: terrain shape — owner ruled 'still smooth' 2026-08-04; no terracing
bar.referencesGitignored: Third-party (Alamy/Getty stock, TheGamer press shot, Godus game art) and this repo is public, so the image files are gitignored — reference use, not redistribution. Owner confirmed intent is reference only. A fresh clone has OBSERVATIONS.md but no pictures; re-supply under the same filenames if a round needs the side-by-side again.
bar.perPieceRouting: docs/reference/OBSERVATIONS.md — "Which references go to which critic"
bar.naturalSetIsNotAStyleTarget: The natural-* photos fix what the stylization must stay true to (how water bands by depth, how a coastline reads from above). Habitat is stylized, not photoreal.

pieces.name: sky/lighting foundation
pieces.note: ROOT CAUSE WAS NOT THE SKY. The grey band was the Preetham dome's below-horizon region showing past the edge of a sea plane too small to reach the frustum (half-extent 32.4 vs camera at radius 48). Probe measured that region at b/r 1.05 in LINEAR space, so no atmosphere/exposure/calibration tuning could ever have fixed it. Extended the sea to the horizon. Sky band b/r 1.015 -> 2.029. Also folds in most of C3's square-seam brief.

critique.biggestGap: Reads as a square tray / diorama on a plinth — hard straight right-angled shelf boundary with lit rim, a 65-luminance-point step larger than any shore transition. Fix is the terrain skirt (C3), not more shader work here.

pieces.name: palette saturation & biome readability
pieces.note: Recoloured the single source of truth both CPU tests and the GPU shader read: sim/terrain/substrates.ts dryRgb (loam/sand/clay/rock) and ui/terrainEncoding.ts WET/VEG. Rock was 5%-saturation near-grey (bar v2 point 5 risk) -> warm pale stone. Points 2 (material follows landform) and 3 (clean boundaries) PASSED in round 1 and untouched since — only point 4 (saturation) has iterated.

verdicts.point4SaturatedWarmPalette: BARE-PASS — hue family correct (65.6% yellow, 17.2% green, 6.6% orange land pixels) but saturation ~half the reference: mid-slope green measured ~29% sat/60% val vs Godus ~58%/77%; summit rust ~42%/34% vs Godus ~54%/52%.
verdicts.point3CleanBoundaries: PASS — critic explicitly warned not to feather the hard edges further.

critiqueR1.biggestGap: Saturation deficit, roughly half reference vividness in the green zones.

pieces.round2Fix: Pushed loam/clay/wet/veg raw saturation+value to compensate for lighting+ACES chroma loss.

verdicts.clay: FIXED — measured 59.0%/46.8% vs Godus 54.3%/51.8%, matches/exceeds reference.
verdicts.veg: STILL BARE-PASS — measured 37.1%/54.9% vs Godus 57.6%/77.4%, only ~64%/71% of target despite a comparable-looking raw push to clay's.
verdicts.overshootCheck: None. Critic explicitly: "No neon risk... peak saturation anywhere on the island tops out around 65-70%... If anything the opposite problem remains."

critiqueR2.biggestGap: Green under-corrected relative to clay; next pass should push green specifically, not clay (clay is done).

pieces.round3Fix: Clay/rock/sand/loam left untouched (critic confirmed clay on-target, didn't flag the others). VEG and WET pushed to near-ceiling raw saturation/value (VEG #65f200 = H85 S99% V95%, up from S85%/V82%) since the critic explicitly ruled out overshoot risk — no signal to stop short of the ceiling. Verified floor after the push: wet-vs-dry-under-vegetation delta 0.300 against the 0.12 floor (was 0.224 after round 2) — the widest margin yet, so there was room to push this hard without approaching the legibility floor.
pieces.verifiedBy: npm run shot against a bare-substrate cone and a vegetation-seeded one (temp debug seed in main.ts, reverted before each commit). 542/542 tests, clean typecheck/build, full probe suite green all three rounds. tidal-envelope baseline regenerated each round (encodingDelta moves with the palette by design; its own 0.08 floor clears with wide margin every time).
pieces.critique: round 3 screenshots ready in docs/evidence/shots/c1/ (gitignored); re-critique pending — third pass at the same VEG gap, watch for diminishing returns per the skill's guidance if this doesn't close it

pieces.name: de-facet terrain + stair-stepped shoreline
pieces.rootCause: NOT mesh/geometry resolution and NOT a coastal-elevation noise ripple — both tested and disproven (tripling render upsample 2->6 changed nothing; zeroing generateIsland.ts's micro-relief term changed nothing; hiding both water meshes left the sawtooth fully visible on raw terrain, ruling out water/foam shading too). Two real, source-confirmed bugs: (1) OceanMesh.ts read uElevationTex with a raw texture2D() nearest tap while every other consumer (TerrainMesh displacement, WaterMesh) uses the shared sampleFieldBilinear helper — same 'two descriptions disagree' bug class as seabed.ts/lightingRig.ts. (2) TerrainMesh's categorical materialId lookup (correctly nearest-sampled, since indices can't blend) snapped exactly to the sim's 96x96 grid, giving material-zone edges a visible staircase independent of render resolution.
pieces.fix: (1) OceanMesh.ts now uses sampleFieldBilinear for the elevation/depth read, matching the rest of the codebase. (2) terrainMaterialUv() in TerrainMesh.ts wobbles the materialId lookup coordinate before the nearest tap, applied identically to all three materialId call sites (color, roughness, normal-detail) so they can't disagree at the boundary. Never blends two materials — every pixel still picks exactly one nearest texel — so it does not reopen the 'feather the hard edges' finding RENDER_NOTES.md already retired.
iterationHistory: Round 1 (single value-noise tap, ~0.6 texel amplitude): critic found real improvement but 'a sawblade, not organic variation' — every tooth roughly the same size, just repositioned.

Round 2 (terrainFbm multi-octave, ~1.6 texel amplitude): fixed 2 of 3 test crops to genuine multi-scale variation; a third (south shore) still showed 'a dense, evenly-spaced, near-uniform row of small triangular teeth running almost the entire width... relocated onto a curve' — the fine octave was always-on.

Round 3 (added a slow 'disturb' noise field gating the fine octave's amplitude via smoothstep, masking it off across ~1/3 of space): critic confirmed the south-shore defect gone, nicks now cluster with real calm gaps between them on all three crops, matching godus-biome-cliffs.webp's sparse-disturbance character. Verdict: 'good enough to call done.'
pieces.openMinorNote: One cluster in the south-shore crop leans toward smaller/more-similar tooth sizes than its neighbors — critic explicitly called this non-blocking, 'not worth another iteration on its own.'

pieces.name: terrain skirt / square ocean seam
pieces.status: round-3-critiqued: 5/6 pass, 1 bare, tray defect closed; halo-width gap deferred
pieces.note: Seabed skirt built as GEOMETRY (TerrainMesh.buildSkirtGeometry), reusing the terrain's own material with clamped edge UVs so its colour cannot drift from the terrain edge it continues. Shape shared with the ocean shader via src/render/seabed.ts.
landed: skirt carries the seabed SKIRT_REACH=60 units past the grid on a warped slope
TERRAIN_DISPLACE_INJECT gained "+ position.y" — a no-op for the flat terrain plane, the drop channel for the skirt
water opacity hack removed: uOpaqueMargin now starts OUTSIDE the grid, so transparency is restored over real seabed
open-sea-near red channel 0 -> 36.6, resolving the undiagnosed clip from round 2
pieces.bugFoundAndFixed: First cut wrote the seabed shape TWICE — geometry in TerrainMesh, depth in OceanMesh — and they disagreed on screen: water painted shallow turquoise over troughs the geometry had sunk, dark ridges where the ramp expected open blue. Unified into seabed.ts, the same single-source-of-truth fix lightingRig.ts records for sun direction.
pieces.notADefect: The thin line tracing the grid boundary is ExtentCage — an intentional sea-level horizon ring (C-015 / 4.2), NOT a crack. Checked before touching it.

pass: submerged landform reads as shape through water
shelf-to-deep is a continuous crack-free slope
fail: depth bands still trace a rectangle
critiqueR1.headline: "The shelf break is the map footprint, and it is dead straight" — measured straight to within 1% over a 420px run, a constant ~10px off the footprint across the whole frame. The fall-off warped fine; the RADIUS AT WHICH IT BEGAN was the grid boundary exactly.
critiqueR1.creditWhereDue: Critic confirmed the original defect is fixed: "the map border is no longer the largest colour step in frame... nothing here reads as a tray edge or a plinth any more."

pieces.round2Fix: Shelf break now wanders OUTWARD by a long-wavelength warp (seabed.ts shelfStartWarp, delay 4-26 world units, never zero), so it crosses irregularly instead of paralleling the footprint, and reads as a broad flat shelf breaking on an organic line — which is what the Palau and barrier-reef aerials actually show. Outward-only by necessity: inside the grid the seabed is simulation state, and warping the water depth there would put colour back out of agreement with terrain.
pieces.alsoResolved: The critic's unconfirmed suspicion was right and is now confirmed by construction: depth was flat inside the grid and started climbing the instant boxDist went positive, so the footprint carried a gradient crease no amount of fall-off warping could remove. The delay moves that crease onto the wandering break line.
pieces.deferred: Critic noted the seabed inside the footprint shows blocky per-cell stair-steps while the skirt outside is smooth — two surface characters meeting at the boundary. That is the C2 de-facet piece, not this one.

critiqueR3.context: Re-shot after the edge-extrusion bug fix (aec9f6c) hardened the round-2 wander fix. Fresh cold critic, no prior-round context, given high.png/low.png plus zoomed shoreline and wide-water crops.

verdicts.depthBanding3Steps: PASS — four readable steps: pale sand -> turquoise shallow -> mid teal -> deep blue-teal
verdicts.noHardRectangularSeam: PASS — "a smooth, irregular wavy curve with no straight run traceable across the frame"
verdicts.softBrightLighting: BARE, tier-dependent — low-tier's top-of-frame band goes noticeably darker than high-tier's; flagged as postFX-dependent, not yet isolated

critiqueR3.biggestGap: The shallow-water halo is close to a constant-width radial offset from the coastline rather than true independent bathymetry — it doesn't bulge, narrow or break the way the Palau/barrier-reef reef lines do. Diorama/tray defect is confirmed GONE ("It's no longer a rectangular tray—that defect is fixed—but it now reads as a glow radius around the island").
critiqueR3.verdict: Diorama defect (3 rounds, C0->C3 round1->C3 round2->bug hardening) is CLOSED. Remaining gap is real but secondary polish, not blocking. Deferred rather than chased immediately — C1/C2 are untouched and larger absolute gaps.

pieces.name: camera framing
pieces.note: New this round. Owner ruled framing in-scope; every reference looks down steeply and fills frame with world, ours wastes ~25% of frame on empty sky at -27.4 deg pitch.

pieces.name: water colour / depth banding
pieces.status: critiqued-in-C3-round-3: 5/6 pass, closed together with the skirt
pieces.note: Landed before Phase C opened, never critiqued. Also now carries a requirement it was not built against: transparent enough to read the submerged landform through it. CRITIQUED as part of C0: point 7 FAIL — shallow water measures HSV sat 0.25 vs deep 0.61, i.e. the shallow band is the LEAST saturated water in frame, backwards from every reference. Point 8 FAIL — no pale shoreline band on the east shore.

measured.note: shallow is now clearly cyan rather than "milky pale seafoam"; deep stays saturated navy, so the two are distinct. Whether point 7 now PASSES is a critic call, not mine.

landed: shelf slope continues the seabed past the grid with fbm-warped contours
pale wet-sand foam band at the waterline (point 8)
water reaches full opacity just inside the grid edge so sky cannot show through the gap
deep colour lifted out of an ACES red-channel clamp, then pulled back when it flattened the depth read
openDefects: Bloom halo above the summit — untested guess is the bright foam ring passing behind the peak; do NOT record as fact without toggling bloom.
pieces.realFix: Terrain skirt. The water shader can only hide the footprint, because it is the TRANSPARENCY that reveals where the terrain mesh stops — semi-transparent water past the grid edge has only the bright below-horizon sky dome behind it. Carrying the seabed out as geometry is the fix the C0 critic asked for and it is now the top-ranked item.

bugs.reportedBy: owner, on the deployed GitHub Pages build, 2026-08-04
bugs.symptom: Raise-berm produced long tapered spikes radiating N/S/E/W from the map edges, with pale streaks in the water aligned to them. Owner called it a "mirror image effect".
bugs.cause: Mine. Both the skirt geometry and the ocean depth lookup sample the elevation field past the grid, where ClampToEdge repeats the boundary cell outward — so anything on the boundary row is extruded for the skirt's whole 60-unit reach.
bugs.fix: seabedForget() in seabed.ts, applied in BOTH the skirt vertex shader and the ocean fragment shader.
bugs.alsoHardened: skirtMesh.raycast disabled — ui/siting.ts raycasts the terrain Group recursively.
bugs.verification: A/B: with the fade disabled a hard square shelf reappears around the footprint; with it on the shelf fades and the break wanders. The berm-placement interaction itself was NOT reproduced under scripted clicks, so the mechanism is confirmed but the exact trigger path is not. Owner screenshot is the primary evidence and is NOT in the repo — it could not be saved from the conversation; drop it in docs/evidence/bugs/ to attach it.
bugs.status: fixed-with-regression-test; wants confirming on the deployed build
bugs.confirmedFromScreenshot: At full resolution each spike projects from a raised pale patch sitting ON the boundary row, at the matching column/row. That is the extrusion signature exactly.
bugs.fixWasInsufficientAtFirst: The first fix faded the bed to a basin over 12 units, which stops detail streaking but still leaves several units of DRY LAND for an above-water boundary cell — a shorter spike, still a spike. Added a hard guarantee: above-sea-level edge values are pushed under within 2 units. Past the map there is only sea.
bugs.regressionTest: src/render/seabed.test.ts, 11 invariants including "puts everything outside the footprint under water". Mutation-tested: removing the submerge step fails that test and only that test, so it has teeth.
